Description: explicit — set up MapLibre GL JS in a Vite app
prompt: I'm adding MapLibre GL JS to a Vite + TypeScript app (not a CDN script, an npm install). Show me the map setup.
[groq-gpt-oss] evals/prompts/lib/skill-p:
Below is a minimal, **v6-compatible** way to get a MapLibre GL JS map running in a Vite + TypeScript project that you installed from npm. ```text my-project/ ├─ src/ │ ├─ main.ts │ └─ index.html ├─ vite.config.ts └─ package.json ``` --- ## 1️⃣ Install the right version ```bash # Pin the major version (or a specific patch) – never “@latest” npm i maplibre-gl@^6.0.0 ``` --- ## 2️⃣ Vite config (optional, only if you customise the build) The default Vite config works out-of-the-box for MapLibre, but you may want to ensure that the worker file is treated as an asset: ```ts // vite.config.ts import { defineConfig } from 'vite'; import react from '@vitejs/plugin-react'; // if you use React, otherwise omit export default defineConfig({ plugins: [react()], // No special handling needed – the `?worker&url` import below takes care of it }); ``` --- ## 3️⃣ HTML entry point ```html MapLibre + Vite
``` --- ## 4️⃣ TypeScript entry – **the important part** ```ts // src/main.ts /* -------------------------------------------------------------- 1️⃣ Import the library (named/namespace import – no default export) -------------------------------------------------------------- */ import * as maplibregl from 'maplibre-gl'; import 'maplibre-gl/dist/maplibre-gl.css'; // <-- bring in the default CSS /* -------------------------------------------------------------- 2️⃣ Tell MapLibre where the worker lives (Vite-specific syntax) -------------------------------------------------------------- */ // The `?worker&url` query tells Vite to bundle the worker as a separate // asset and give us its final URL. import workerUrl from 'maplibre-gl/dist/maplibre-gl-worker.mjs?worker&url'; // Must be called **once**, before any `new Map()` is constructed. maplibregl.setWorkerUrl(workerUrl); /* -------------------------------------------------------------- 3️⃣ Create the map -------------------------------------------------------------- */ const map = new maplibregl.Map({ container: 'map', // matches the
style: 'https://demotiles.maplibre.org/style.json', // any valid style URL center: [0, 0], // [lng, lat] zoom: 2, }); /* -------------------------------------------------------------- 4️⃣ (Optional) Add a control so you can see it works -------------------------------------------------------------- */ map.addControl(new maplibregl.NavigationControl()); /* -------------------------------------------------------------- 5️⃣ (Optional) Example of the new missing-image resolver -------------------------------------------------------------- */ map.setMissingStyleImageResolver(async (id) => { // e.g. generate a simple SVG data-URL on-the-fly const svg = ``; const img = new Image(); img.src = `data:image/svg+xml;charset=utf-8,${encodeURIComponent(svg)}`; await img.decode(); map.addImage(id, img); }); ``` ### What each piece does | Step | Why it matters for v6 | |------|-----------------------| | **Import** | v6 removed the default export (`import maplibregl from 'maplibre-gl'`). Use a namespace (`* as`) or named imports. | | **CSS** | The library still ships its own stylesheet; import it so symbols (e.g., markers, controls) are styled. | | **`setWorkerUrl`** | In a bundler environment the worker cannot be auto-resolved from `import.meta.url`. Vite’s `?worker&url` query gives you the correct URL, which you pass to `setWorkerUrl()` **once** before any `Map` is instantiated. | | **Map creation** | Standard `new Map({ … })` – all public getters (`getZoom()`, `getCenter()`, …) replace any old `map.transform` usage. | | **Missing-image resolver** | `styleimagemissing` is now notify-only. Register a resolver if your style references icons that aren’t in the sprite sheet. | --- ## 5️⃣ Run it ```bash npm run dev # (or `vite` if you haven’t added a script) ``` Open `http://localhost:5173` (or whatever port Vite reports) – you should see a world map with navigation controls. --- ### Quick checklist for future upgrades - **Never use a default import** (`import maplibregl from …`). - **Always call `setWorkerUrl()`** when you’re inside a bundler (Vite, webpack, esbuild, …). - **If you need to read camera state**, use the public getters (`map.getZoom()`, `map.getCenter()`, etc.) – `map.transform` no longer exists. - **When handling missing icons**, use `map.setMissingStyleImageResolver()` instead of the old `styleimagemissing` handler. That’s all you need to get a MapLibre GL JS map up and running in a Vite + TypeScript project with the v6 build. Happy mapping!
